title: Shor's 1997 SIAM paper gives polynomial-time quantum algorithms for factoring and discrete logarithms
summary: Peter W. Shor's paper, published in SIAM Journal on Computing in October 1997, presents efficient randomized algorithms that factor integers and find discrete logarithms in polynomial time on a hypothetical quantum computer.
body: In a paper published in the SIAM Journal on Computing in October 1997 (DOI 10.1137/S0097539795293172), Peter W. Shor presented polynomial-time algorithms for prime factorization and discrete logarithms on a quantum computer. The peer-reviewed paper is an expanded journal version of earlier work; a preprint version was submitted to arXiv on 30 August 1995 and revised on 25 January 1996. The preprint's abstract states: "This paper considers factoring integers and finding discrete logarithms, two problems which are generally thought to be hard on a classical computer and have been used as the basis of several proposed cryptosystems." It also states: "Efficient randomized algorithms are given for these two problems on a hypothetical quantum computer. These algorithms take a number of steps polynomial in the input size, e.g., the number of digits of the integer to be factored."
